title: Closing a project: purpose, objectives, planned and premature
blurb: Explain why every project needs a fixed closing point, what closing a project must achieve, and how planned and premature closures differ.
question: A project board decides to stop a project halfway through because its business case is no longer valid. Who makes that call, and is the closing a project process still needed?

teach.h: A fixed point to finish properly
teach.body: Formally: closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed, and at which the team recognizes that the objectives in the PID (or approved changes to them) have been achieved. If there is a reason to close early, it makes sure the project is closed in an orderly way. In plain English: the project does not just fizzle out. Someone checks the users have accepted what was built, then the project formally ends.

items: Check that users have accepted the project product.
Make sure the business can support the products once the project has closed.
Review how the project performed against its baselines.
Assess benefits already realized and update the benefits management approach to cover post-project benefits reviews.
Make provision for all open issues and risks, with follow-on action recommendations.
In a premature close, make sure the project is closed in an orderly way rather than simply abandoned.

teach.h: Closing sits inside the final stage
teach.caption: Closing a project is the last part of the final stage, not a stage of its own.

rows.label: Trigger
values: Premature close notice from the board

rows.label: Typical reason
values: For example, business case no longer valid

rows.label: Extra work
values: Salvage useful work, make products safe

teach.caption: The project manager prepares for closure; the project board authorizes it.

teach.h: Why a clear end beats a slow drift into use

rows.label: Ownership passes to the people who will use the products

teach.note: This is true even when a project closes early.

teach.body: Marlowe Shipping is building a vessel tracking system when a regulator announces a free national service that does the same job. Executive Fiona Clarke's board decides the business case is no longer valid and triggers a premature close. Project manager Kwame Asante still runs closing a project, tailored: he saves the data integration work for reuse, makes the half-built software safe, records what is finished and what is abandoned, then requests closure from the board.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) The project BOARD triggers a premature close, not the PM. (2) A premature close still uses closing a project, tailored. (3) Closing a project is inside the final stage, not a separate stage. (4) The project plans benefits reviews after closure; it does not carry them out.

items: Purpose: a fixed point to confirm acceptance of the project product and that objectives have been met, or an orderly early close.
Objectives include user acceptance, ongoing support, review against baselines, benefits assessment and follow-on actions.
Triggered by the project end approaching, or by the board's premature close notice.
The PM prepares closure; the board authorizes it in directing a project.
A clear end stops costs, transfers ownership and releases the team.

summary: You can now state the purpose and objectives of closing a project, explain why a clear end matters and contrast planned with premature closure. You can also say who triggers each and who authorizes closure.

A.q: Which is a purpose of the closing a project process?
options: Help the board decide whether to start the next stage
Give a fixed point to confirm acceptance of the product
Control the link between the PM and the team managers
Make sure there is a viable and worthwhile project
A.why: Closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed (manual 19.1).

whyNot.0: Supporting the next-stage decision is managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.2: Controlling the PM to team manager link is managing product delivery.
whyNot.3: Checking for a viable and worthwhile project is starting up a project.

A.q: Who can trigger a premature closure of a project?
options: The project manager
The team manager
Project assurance
The project board
A.why: The project board may trigger a premature close, for example if the business case is no longer valid (manual 19.3).

whyNot.0: The PM prepares the closure but does not trigger a premature close.
whyNot.1: Team managers work in managing product delivery and do not make closure decisions.
whyNot.2: Project assurance supports the board but does not decide to close the project.

A.q: Where does closing a project sit in the project lifecycle?
options: At the end of the final stage
In a separate closure stage
After a final stage boundary
After the board's closure notice
A.why: Closing a project is the last part of the final stage; it is not a stage of its own.

whyNot.1: Closure is not its own stage; it is planned within the final stage.
whyNot.2: Managing a stage boundary is not used at the end of the final stage.
whyNot.3: The board's closure notification follows closing a project; it does not come before it.

B.q:
Which two statements are objectives of the closing a project process?
1. Prepare the stage plan for the final stage.
2. Check user acceptance of the project product.
3. Ensure the business can support the products after the project has closed.
4. Provide authority to close the project.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: Checking user acceptance (2) and ensuring the business can support the products after closure (3) are objectives of closing a project (manual 19.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 belongs to managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 belongs to managing a stage boundary and statement 4 to directing a project.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is an objective of directing a project, where the board authorizes closure.

B.q: A project is being closed prematurely. What should happen to the closing a project process?
options: It is still run, tailored to the situation
It is replaced by an exception plan
It is skipped, as the work has stopped
It is handed to the business layer to run
B.why: If a project is closed prematurely, closing a project still needs to be run, though it may be tailored (manual 19.3).

whyNot.1: An exception plan replaces a plan that is forecast to exceed tolerance; it does not close a project.
whyNot.2: Skipping closure risks abandoning the project instead of closing it in an orderly way.
whyNot.3: The PM still prepares closure; the business layer receives the closure notification.

B.q: Why is a clear project end better than a slow drift into use?
options: Benefits reviews can be completed by the PM
The board can approve another stage plan
Project costs stop and ownership is transferred
Team managers can extend their work packages
B.why: A clear end signals that project costs should stop, ownership passes to the users and the team can disband (manual 19.3).

whyNot.0: Post-project benefits reviews are carried out by the business after closure, not by the PM.
whyNot.1: No further stage plans are approved once the project closes.
whyNot.3: Work packages end with the project; they are not extended by closing.

C.q: Who prepares the project for closure, and who authorizes the closure?
options: The board prepares; the business layer authorizes
The PM prepares; the senior user authorizes
The team manager prepares; the PM authorizes
The PM prepares; the project board authorizes
C.why: The PM prepares closure in closing a project; the project board authorizes it in directing a project (authorize project closure).

whyNot.0: The board does not prepare closure; the business layer is notified of it.
whyNot.1: Closure is authorized by the project board as a whole, not the senior user alone.
whyNot.2: Team managers do not prepare project closure, and the PM cannot authorize it.

C.q: Which objective of closing a project concerns benefits, and where are later benefits reviews planned?
options: Realize all benefits before closure; in the end project report
Assess benefits realized so far; in the benefits management approach
Assess benefits realized so far; in the lessons report
Measure every benefit after handover; in the project plan
C.why: Closing a project assesses benefits already realized and updates the benefits management approach to include post-project benefits reviews (manual 19.2).

whyNot.0: Many benefits arise after closure; the project does not need to realize them all first.
whyNot.2: Lessons reports pass on lessons, not the plan for benefits reviews.
whyNot.3: Benefits are measured by the business after closure, and the reviews are planned in the benefits management approach.

C.q: Which closing a project objective applies specifically to a premature close?
options: Check user acceptance of the project product
Review performance against the baselines
Make sure the project is not simply abandoned
Address open issues with follow-on actions
C.why: For a premature close, closing a project ensures the project is closed in an orderly way and not simply abandoned (manual 19.2).

whyNot.0: Checking user acceptance is a general objective of closing a project.
whyNot.1: Reviewing performance against baselines applies to every closure.
whyNot.3: Follow-on action recommendations apply to every closure.

reteach.title: Moving out of a rented flat
reteach.question: When a tenancy ends, why not just leave the keys on the table and walk away?

blocks.body: A proper move-out has a fixed checkout: the landlord inspects and accepts the flat, bills stop, the keys pass over and any snags get a note for follow-up. If you must leave early, you still check out, just faster and with some things left to sort. Closing a project is that checkout, planned or premature.

blocks.text: The landlord (board) decides on an early end and signs off the checkout. The tenant (PM) prepares it.

explain.body: The heart of closing a project is a fixed point where acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the objectives in the PID are recognized as achieved.

test.q: What does closing a project provide a fixed point for?
options: Confirming acceptance of the project product
Agreeing the tolerances for the final stage
Approving the project initiation documentation
Appointing the project management team
test.why: Closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed (manual 19.1).

whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set by the board when it authorizes a stage.
whyNot.2: The PID is approved when the board authorizes the project.
whyNot.3: The team is appointed in starting up a project.

explain.body: Open issues and risks must not vanish at closure. Each gets a follow-on action recommendation so the business knows what still needs handling.

test.q: What should happen to open issues and risks when a project closes?
options: They are moved into the next stage plan
They are escalated in an exception report
They are closed on the project log and dropped
They are given follow-on action recommendations
test.why: An objective of closing a project is to make provision for all open issues and risks with follow-on action recommendations (manual 19.2).

whyNot.0: There is no next stage after closure.
whyNot.1: Exception reports deal with forecast tolerance breaches, not handover of open items.
whyNot.2: Dropping them would leave the business unaware of work still needed.

explain.body: When the board triggers an early close, the PM records the request, salvages anything useful, makes products safe and agrees what is completed or abandoned.

items: Agree what is completed or abandoned

test.q: Which action is part of preparing a premature closure?
options: Request authority to start the final stage
Salvage useful work and make products safe
Prepare the next stage plan for the board
Raise an exception report to the business
test.why: Preparing a premature closure includes salvaging useful work, making products safe and agreeing what is completed or abandoned (manual 19.4.2).

whyNot.0: A premature close ends the project; it does not start another stage.
whyNot.2: Next stage plans belong to managing a stage boundary.
whyNot.3: The decision to close has already been made by the board.

explain.body: In a planned closure, controlling a stage triggers closing a project as the project end approaches in the final stage.

test.q: In a planned closure, which process triggers closing a project?
options: Managing a stage boundary, after the final stage
Starting up a project, through the project brief
Controlling a stage, as the project end approaches
Managing product delivery, on work completion
test.why: Closing a project is triggered from controlling a stage as the project end approaches in the final stage.

whyNot.0: Managing a stage boundary is not used at the end of the final stage.
whyNot.1: Starting up a project happens before the project begins.
whyNot.3: Work package completion returns to controlling a stage, not directly to closure.
